_meta.anthropic/searchHint: drag drop slider mouse press move release chromium select

description:
Press the left mouse button at a start point, move to an end point, and release: a desktop mouse drag in a Chromium app, with mouse moves interpolated at ~60fps. All positions are fractions of the window width/height (not pixels), the same space as gesture-tap and describe, except that exactly 1.0 lands one pixel inside the window edge.
Use for slider thumbs, drag-and-drop, text selection, or draggable UI elements. Dragging never scrolls content on desktop; use gesture-scroll for lists/pages. Chromium only: on iOS/Android use gesture-swipe.
Returns { dragged: true, timestampMs }. Fails if the Chromium CDP session is not reachable for the given device.

durationMs.description: Total drag duration in milliseconds (default 300); the button stays down this long. Maximum: 10000.

momentum.description: Whether the drag releases with momentum; default true (a constant-speed drag). false decelerates into the release point, so an app that derives a fling from the release velocity (carousels, drag libraries) applies little to no momentum: use it when the drag must stop where it was aimed. Under ~100ms durationMs some fling survives; keep the default 300 when the fling must be fully suppressed.

name: gesture-drag
